title: The Year-End Swap
intro: Text 1 is a poster for a uniform and textbook swap run by a school’s parent support group.

visual.text: Outgrown it? Someone else is about to grow into it.
Pass on your uniforms and textbooks. Pick up what you need for next year.

A long table in a school hall is piled with folded uniforms sorted by size. A tall Secondary 4 boy hands a stack of textbooks to a much smaller boy, who is grinning and already holding the top book open.

New uniforms and a full booklist are a heavy bill at the start of every year. Yet in most homes, last year’s books sit in a box, and shirts that no longer fit hang at the back of the wardrobe. Bring them to the Swap. Whatever you bring, someone will use — and whatever you need, you take home free.

visual.title: What we accept
items: School uniforms and PE attire, washed and without tears
Textbooks on next year’s booklist — notes in pencil are fine
School shoes and bags in good condition
Sorry, no workbooks that have been written in

visual.text: “My brother’s old Chemistry textbook had his notes in the margins. They explained things better than the book did.” — Aditi, Secondary 3
There is no need to bring something in order to take something. Nobody will ask.
Saturday, 22 November · 9 am to 1 pm · School Hall

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a forum post by Wen Hui, a Secondary 2 student, about using second-hand textbooks.
paragraphs: Every December, my mother sits at the kitchen table with the booklist and a calculator, and goes very quiet. With three of us in school, the books and uniforms for January cost her more than she spends on groceries in a month. So last year, when a neighbour offered us her son’s old books, I said thank you and felt secretly embarrassed. I did not want anyone in class to notice that my books were not new.

That feeling lasted about two weeks. Inside the Geography textbook, the boy had drawn tiny arrows and diagrams beside every chapter, and they made the hard parts make sense. Now I am the one keeping my books neat, because I already know which girl on my block will get them next.

options.label: B

options.label: C

scheme.answer: Things students have outgrown can be passed on, free, to others who need them.

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support the headline ‘Outgrown it? Someone else is about to grow into it.’?

scheme.answer: A tall older boy hands his textbooks to a much smaller boy who is eager to use them, showing that what one student has outgrown goes straight to a younger one who needs it.
accept: The big Secondary 4 boy is passing his old books to a small boy who is already reading one, so the things one student no longer needs are about to be used by another.

seeds.text: The picture shows a tall Sec 4 boy giving his textbooks to a much smaller boy, so the older boy has outgrown them and the younger boy is going to grow into them, like the headline says.
The older student passes his books to a younger kid who is happy and already opening one, so the old books will be used again by someone who needs them.
It shows that the small boy is buying the books from the older boy at a cheap price.
It shows students at the swap who look happy.
